clue.text: Two necessities for tennis game

parts.note: a tennis match cannot be played without a net across the court
nor without a ball to hit over it

explanation.surface: Someone lists the two pieces of kit a tennis player cannot do without.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at tennis, but the two essentials, net and ball, join to name a different sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team sport, mostly played by women in Britain and the Commonwealth, so it is a kind of game.

clue.text: Emerging from China's central region

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something newly appearing from the middle of China.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'region' as the definition, but the answer means 'Emerging'; the run spans 'China's central'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into being, beginning to develop.

clue.text: Vehicular entrance

definitions.meaning: read as en-trance, to fill with delight, to enrapture

explanation.surface: A way for vehicles to get in.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport means vehicles carrying goods or people, and also to carry away with delight, to enrapture.

clue.text: Moving broadcast about saint

indicators.note: about says the broadcast goes round the saint

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A touching programme about a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' looks like 'touching'; it means up and about.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, in motion.

clue.text: Realise about one pound is overdue

indicators.note: about means the overdue word goes round one pound

parts.note: late means overdue
I is the Roman numeral for one
a quid is British slang for a pound

explanation.surface: Someone becomes aware that a pound is owed and late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Realise' looks like 'understand'; it is the financial sense of converting assets to cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To liquidate assets is to turn them into cash, which is to realise them.

clue.text: Evidence that Tommy's worried about money

indicators.note: about means the rearranged name goes around the money
worried suggests the letters of the name are fretted into a new order

parts.note: the possessive is read with its S as a letter
P, for pence, is a small sum of British money

explanation.surface: A sign that a soldier (a Tommy) is anxious about his finances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges TOMMYS into SYMTOM, and 'about' puts that around P to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is a sign or indication of an illness or problem, so it is evidence of it.

clue.text: Appropriate dates, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says a word for dates is said out loud

parts.note: someone who dates another sees them, as in going out together

explanation.surface: Fitting dates that sound right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like the adjective 'fitting'; it is the verb, to take.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate something is to take it for oneself, to grab it.

clue.text: Produce a film? I neglected to take action

indicators.note: neglected means the I is left out of the phrase

parts.note: to make a movie is to produce a film

explanation.surface: A film producer admits he failed to do anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I neglected' reads as a confession; it drops I from MAKE A MOVIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a move is to begin acting, to do something.

clue.text: Fawn resembling an amphibian?

definitions.meaning: to fawn is to flatter servilely, so as a noun one who fawns
toad with Y added makes an adjective, toad-like, the question mark flagging the made-up word

explanation.surface: A young deer that looks a bit like a frog.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady is a sycophant who fawns, and toad-y jokingly means like a toad.

clue.text: Diffidence shown in two ways, one unknown

parts.note: a mode is a way of doing something
ST, street, is a way or road
Y is one of the unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: Shyness displayed in a couple of manners.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra X, Y and Z stand for unknown quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: Modesty is shyness or reserve about oneself, which is diffidence.

clue.text: Reversing vehicles that's clever

indicators.note: Reversing tells us to read the word for vehicles from back to front

parts.note: trams are vehicles running on rails in the street

explanation.surface: A neat trick of backing up some vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversing' turns TRAMS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and clever are synonyms for quick-witted.

clue.text: Dangerous' terrain with rapids ahead

indicators.note: ahead places the rapid ones before the word for with

parts.note: quick means rapid, so rapids (plural adjective as noun) gives quicks
and joins one thing with another

explanation.surface: A warning about risky ground with white water just in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rapids' is read as rapid ones, and 'ahead' puts them first. The apostrophe after 'Dangerous' is a speck on the printed page, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicksand is loose wet sand that swallows anything heavy, ground that is a hazard to walk on.

clue.text: A vet in America is out of work

parts.note: ex means out of or from, as in ex-directory
service is work done for someone

explanation.surface: An American veteran finds himself unemployed.
explanation.walkthrough: In America 'vet' is short for veteran, a former member of the armed forces, which is what ex-service describes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ex-service person, a former soldier, is what Americans call a vet, short for veteran.

clue.text: A ship after passing through the Gulf

indicators.note: after places the ship following the word for passing through

parts.note: by means via, passing through a place on the way
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A vessel has come through the Persian Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Gulf' looks like the Persian Gulf; it is a chasm. 'after' sets the ship behind the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulf can be a deep chasm or bottomless pit, a synonym of abyss.

clue.text: Red-head standing out of the crowd wearing this!

indicators.note: standing out of means the red-head stands outside and is taken away from the crowd

parts.note: a throng is a crowd

indicators.note: head here means the first letter of the word red, joined to it by the hyphen

explanation.surface: A redhead conspicuous in the crowd because of skimpy clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing out of' removes R from THRONG. 'this' plus 'wearing' points at a garment worn, the skimpy item that made the redhead stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a skimpy piece of underwear or swimwear, the item someone would be wearing here.

clue.text: A dog — Hamlet, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a very large breed of dog
Shakespeare's Hamlet is a prince of Denmark, so a notable Dane

explanation.surface: Is the hound named after the Prince of Denmark?
explanation.definitionFit: A Great Dane is a giant dog breed, and Hamlet is a famous Danish prince, a great Dane.

clue.text: How rarity can be made safe

indicators.note: can be made says the letters of the phrase are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A question about turning something rare into something secure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be made' rearranges the letters of HOW RARITY.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft judged airworthy is fit to fly, that is, safe.

clue.text: Memo about a rest

indicators.note: about means the memo goes round the a

parts.note: a memo is a reminder

explanation.surface: A note concerning a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside REMINDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, the rest.

clue.text: The aurochs — it is in the dictionary

indicators.note: is in tells us the word for it sits inside the other piece

parts.note: the urus is another name for the aurochs, an extinct wild ox
SA, sex appeal, is crossword 'it'

explanation.surface: Someone finds the extinct wild ox listed in a dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is SA, sex appeal, a crossword convention. A thesaurus is a dictionary of synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book of synonyms, a kind of dictionary.

clue.text: Abreast, and going the right way

definitions.meaning: in sailing, something at right angles to the keel, level with the ship's side, is abreast
in aviation, flying along a radio guide beam means being on course

explanation.surface: Side by side and heading in the correct direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: at right angles to a ship, or following a guiding radio beam and so on course.

clue.text: Had greater fire power to shout abroad

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A gun had more firepower than a shout could carry overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges TO SHOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshoot someone is to shoot better or more than them, past tense here.

clue.text: In the result, you'll find me correct

indicators.note: In tells us me sits inside the word for the result

parts.note: the end is the result or outcome

explanation.surface: Someone claims the outcome will show them to be right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you'll find' is a link; 'In' signals the container, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct its errors.

clue.text: County agreed over girl

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the agreed word above the girl

parts.note: done, as in 'done!', means agreed in a deal
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A county consented to have a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Donegal is a county in the north-west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Donegal is one of the counties of Ireland.

clue.text: Bird without bill is silent

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the bird goes round the bill

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A bird with no beak cannot sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense 'outside', not 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means unspoken, understood without words, so silent.

clue.text: Shrub with flower buds that can be cut

definitions.meaning: a Mediterranean shrub whose flower buds are pickled and eaten
a lively leap, as in the idiom to cut one

explanation.surface: A bush whose buds can be pruned.
explanation.definitionFit: The caper bush has edible pickled buds, and one cuts a caper, a playful skipping leap.

clue.text: Tribal leader has a reformed thief and murderer around

indicators.note: around tells us the murderer is placed outside the reshaped thief

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in the Bible

indicators.note: reformed means the thief's letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: A clan chief keeps company with a thief gone straight and a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' gives HIEFT from the thief, and 'around' wraps the Biblical murderer about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chieftain is the head of a tribe or clan.

clue.text: Vessels start to congregate, a large gathering

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: a raft of things is a large number of them

explanation.surface: Ships begin to gather in a big flotilla.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' takes C from 'congregate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft as a plural means boats or ships, vessels.

clue.text: The fuzz makes a mistake

definitions.meaning: fuzz here is soft downy material
to bungle a line or shot

explanation.surface: The police slip up.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluff is soft fuzz, and to fluff something is to bungle it.

clue.text: Casual fellow loses his head when facing danger

indicators.note: loses his head means the fellow drops his first letter

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
a hazard is a danger

explanation.surface: An offhand man is beheaded when confronting peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses his head' drops C from the fellow, and 'when facing' just sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Haphazard means random or careless, without plan, a sense of casual.

clue.text: Forwards from United not recognisable in Gunners' strip

indicators.note: Forwards here are the front letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A football report: United's forwards cannot be told apart in Arsenal's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forwards' looks like football players; it means the leading letters. Gunners is the nickname of Arsenal football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To unrig a ship is to strip it of its rigging.

clue.text: Harrow people are in the wrong

indicators.note: are in tells us the people sit inside the word for the wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are people

explanation.surface: People from Harrow (a London district with a famous school) have made an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harrow' looks like the place; it is the verb meaning distress.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrow is to distress greatly, as to torment does.

clue.text: Fashionable seal fur gets thumbs down

indicators.note: Fashionable read as able to be fashioned, so the letters are shaped anew

explanation.surface: Sealskin as a fashion item meets disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashionable' rearranges SEAL FUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving the thumbs down is a gesture of rejection, a refusal.
